findings.title: "Independent of ... 320" is false — the generated documents collide with the metrology audit harness's file globs
findings.description:
The Dependencies section asserts "Independent of 140, 180, 240, 260, 280, 300, and **320** — no pipeline, judging, or agent-provider machinery is involved." Initiative 320's audit harness does not consume pipeline machinery — it consumes *filename patterns in `project-documents/user/analysis/`*, which is exactly where both capabilities write.

I verified in `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py`:
- `_AUDIT_FILE_GLOBS = ("project-documents/user/analysis/*-analysis.*.md", ...)`. `943-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` and `944-analysis.overview.md` both match.
- `find_audit_file()` returns `max(fresh, key=mtime)` over that glob. After a comprehension or overview run, the freshest match is the squadron-generated document, not the audit file; the harness then reads it and raises `AuditBlockMissingError` → `AuditRunFailure.BLOCK_MISSING`, persisting nothing and wasting a 5–20 minute, high-token audit run.
- `_AUDIT_ARTIFACT_PATTERN` matches `project-documents/user/analysis/\d+-analysis\..+\.md` as an untracked `??` line and treats it as "the audit's own output". So a comprehension/overview document sitting untracked in that directory makes `preflight_project(require_clean=True)` pass on a tree that is *not* clean — silently weakening the variance-series precondition that 320/323 were built to guarantee. A noise floor measured across untracked document additions is not a floor.

The architecture needs to either name its files so they cannot match `*-analysis.*.md` (a different topic segment or directory), or declare the 320 interaction and specify the harness change. As written, the document's own "no new directory" decision is the cause.

findings.title: Tracking an auto-updated, machine-generated knowledge graph dirties the worktree that other initiatives require clean
findings.description:
"Ignore the scratch, track the artifacts" requires `knowledge-graph.json`, `meta.json`, `config.json` and `.understandignore` to stay tracked because they are "durable project knowledge" and staleness should be "visible in review." Two problems the document does not address:

1. The output contract table itself says `config.json` carries `autoUpdate` — read-only for squadron, and squadron explicitly refuses to drive the plugin ("Squadron installs the marketplace plugin" is a non-goal; "never written by squadron"). An auto-updating tool writing into a file squadron mandates be tracked means every background re-analysis produces a large modified tracked file. `_is_audit_artifact()` exempts only untracked `analysis/*-analysis.*.md` paths and only `??` lines, so ` M .understand-anything/knowledge-graph.json` *does* appear in `offending` → `AuditPreflightError: the worktree is dirty`. Capability 1 therefore blocks 320's variance series simply by existing in the same repo. This is the same failure class the harness comment calls out ("Git collapses a wholly-untracked directory ... so every prefix of both locations must match") — the pattern was written for the audit's own output, not for a second producer.
2. No size assessment. The plugin graph contains per-node `summary` and `tags[]` text for every file node; for the "200–1000 files" repos the document cites as the target engagement, this is a multi-MB, non-reviewable generated blob committed into the repo, whose diff churn defeats the stated purpose of "staleness visible in review." Committing `meta.json` (small) achieves that; committing the graph does not.

findings.title: The read discipline is not implementable as a skill-only, no-code capability
findings.description: "**Read discipline:** the graph is large. Grep for the needed section before reading; never load the whole file into context." Then step 3 of the Flow requires extracting `project`, `layers[]`, `tour[]` and *file-level nodes with their `summary`, `filePath`, and `complexity`*. `knowledge-graph.json` is a single JSON document; section-oriented grep works only if upstream emits one-object-per-line pretty-printed JSON, and filtering `nodes[]` down to the nine file-level types while dropping `function:`/`class:` nodes is not something grep-then-read can do — either the file is line-per-node (so `nodes[]` is the bulk of the file and the "needed subset" is most of it) or it is minified (so any grep returns a single unreadable line). The document names no extraction tool (no `jq` requirement, no helper script), while the Scope says "No pipeline actions ... no changes to the executor" and the deprecated slice 344 notes the plugin is Node-based (33 MB dependency), so even `jq` availability is unaccounted for. I could not verify the plugin's JSON formatting from this repo — the marketplace plugin is not vendored here — so the point is specifically that the document asserts a retrieval strategy it does not substantiate and whose failure mode is "load the whole graph into context," the thing it forbids. If a mechanical extraction step is needed, it is code, and the "skill-level transform, no machinery" framing hides a complexity cliff.

findings.title: Initiative-plan candidates have no output location, docType, or index rule, and the index allocator is undefined for both capabilities
findings.description:
The Outputs section names concrete paths for the concept doc and the comprehension analysis, then says initiative-plan candidates are "offered for PM review. Written only on explicit confirmation" — without saying *where they are written, with what `docType`, or with what index*. This is load-bearing and contradicts the Output Conventions section:
- `project-documents/user/project-guides/` holds exactly one initiative plan (`001-initiative-plan.squadron.md`, verified); candidates are not the plan, so they cannot occupy `001-`.
- Output Conventions promises "No new directory, no new docType", and `src/squadron/documents/schema.py` `DocType` is a 15-value fixed enum with no candidate type — so candidates must be smuggled into either `initiative-plan` (falsely claiming commitment status, and `cf validate frontmatter` won't catch the lie) or `analysis` in the 900 band. Neither is stated.
- "derived from layer boundaries and complexity clustering, offered for PM review" is the "step 3: magic happens" of this design: no candidate schema, no effort/scope signal, no tie-break when layers don't suggest a coherent initiative.

Separately, neither capability specifies *how the next index is chosen*. "incrementing per run like the existing `940`/`941`/`942` series" describes the observed result, not the rule — no scan-for-max, no collision handling when capability (a)'s comprehension doc and capability (b)'s overview are generated in the same session and both take `943`.

findings.title: "Overflow into 950+ is sanctioned" contradicts "no change to `file-naming-conventions.md`"
findings.description: Two adjacent paragraphs take opposite positions: "**no change to `file-naming-conventions.md`**" and "**Overflow into 950+ is sanctioned** ... generated documents take remaining slots in the 900 band as needed rather than stopping at 949." The 940–949 reservation is a claim about a file this initiative explicitly says it will not modify — and that file is owned by the `ai-project-guide` submodule (`project-documents/ai-project-guide` is a git submodule per `.gitmodules`; I could not read it because the submodule is not checked out in this working tree, so the actual reservation text is unverified). `project-documents/DEVLOG.md` records precedent that cross-repo convention changes are "recorded, not crossed" and require a follow-up in the guide repo, and `src/squadron/documents/schema.py` plus slice 172's drift test establish that the canonical enums are mirrored into squadron code and *tested against the guide file*. Declarding unilateral sanction to consume a band the convention may assign elsewhere ("The 900 band is heavily used and its subdivision may need to be widened or re-cut later") is exactly the deferred decision this section claims doesn't exist. Either the overflow needs a guide-repo change (and then "no convention change" is false, and it is a dependency), or the document should stop inventing indices outside the reserved range.

findings.title: Derived documents inherit the audit's independent-sample indexing, which is wrong for a commitment-facing artifact
findings.description: The tech-debt-audit convention is justified as "each run is an independent sample rather than a revision of the last." Capability 2 adopts the same indexing for the client overview while asserting the opposite semantics: "The stakeholder document restates existing approved artifacts" and "Client document is derived, not authored." A derived document is by definition a *revision*, so a fresh index per run produces N equally-valid client-facing overviews with no supersession marker, no "as-of" date in the field schema, and no rule for what happens to `944-analysis.overview.md` when the initiative plan changes. The stated failure mode this design most fears — "a client document that overstates progress is a liability" — is realized precisely by handing a stakeholder a stale revision that nothing marks as stale. The design goals ("Leave the working tree clean", "derived, not authored") imply an overwrite/supersede policy; the document supplies neither, and Open Questions defers only capability (a)'s interview wording and the `[INFERRED]` reuse, not this.

findings.title: Which repository and which `project:` the generated documents belong to is never decided
findings.description: The input contract is anchored at `$PROJECT_ROOT/.understand-anything/`; the outputs are anchored at `project-documents/user/...` with a `{project}` placeholder that is never defined. The Motivation is a foreign codebase ("Real engagements start from an existing codebase with no planning artifacts"), and the "squadron's own repo is an instance" example is a *different* case. For a target repo that is not squadron, the document does not say: whether the concept/comprehension docs land in the target repo's `project-documents/user/` or in squadron's; what `project:` frontmatter value they carry (the target's name vs `squadron`); what `initiative:`/`index:` they claim, given that frontmatter requires those fields and the target has no initiative plan yet (that's the whole point). This matters mechanically, not just editorially: `cf validate frontmatter` checks the required universal fields (per slice 172 and `frontmatter_gate.py`), and `src/squadron/metrology/identity.derive_project_id` keys the store on the audited project — a concept doc written into squadron's tree *about* another repo will be read back as squadron's own concept. The capability-2 flow has the same gap: it reads the initiative plan of "the" project, which is ambiguous when both a client repo and a squadron workspace are in play.

findings.title: Capability (b)'s first-party command rollout is unaccounted for, and a new `commands/sq/` file breaks exact-set test fixtures
findings.description:
Delivery says capability (b) ships "as a first-party command in `commands/sq/`" with no other change. Verified consequences the document does not mention:
- `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py` asserts an **exact set**: `EXPECTED_FILES = {analysis.md, auth.md, list.md, review.md, run.md, shutdown.md, spawn.md, summary.md, task.md}` with `installed == EXPECTED_FILES`, plus `len(... glob("*.md")) == 9` at lines 58, 115 and 123. Adding `commands/sq/overview.md` fails those assertions until they're edited — a code/test change the architecture's "no CLI change" framing doesn't cover for (b).
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md:59` hard-codes "9 command(s) at ~/.claude/commands/sq".
- `src/squadron/cli/commands/doctor_checks.py::check_slash_commands` only counts `*.md` and reports OK if any exist — it does not verify membership. So an upgraded user who never re-runs `sq install-commands` gets "✓ slash commands 9 command(s)" and no `/sq:overview`, and doctor cannot tell them. The document should specify the rollout/verification step (re-run install, or a membership check) rather than assuming presence.
- Dependencies lists "**[100]** — CLI command registration for any command surface." Both surfaces are pure markdown: `install.py::install_commands` copies every `*.md` under every subdir of `commands/`, and the pack installer globs `*.md` (`installer.py::_install_prefix`). No Typer registration is involved for either capability, so the stated [100] dependency appears spurious and should be dropped or re-justified — a fake dependency in an architecture doc is what makes slice planning allocate work that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Precondition and error handling stop at "file exists"; the realistic failure modes are not addressed
findings.description:
Flow step 1 verifies "the plugin is installed and `knowledge-graph.json` exists. If the graph is missing, report the exact command to run (`/understand`) and stop." What it does not cover:
- **Plugin install detection.** There is no mechanism for a markdown skill to inspect Claude Code's plugin registry; the observable signal is the graph file. The Non-Goals promise "The skill detects absence and instructs," which as stated is unimplementable, and per CLAUDE.md's hallucination-trap rule ("If no such line is present, stop with an error") the check must be reduced to a concrete, observable file/section presence — otherwise the skill will pattern-match a plausible "installed" state.
- **Present-but-malformed or partial graph.** The plugin writes the graph across a 7-phase pipeline; an interrupted run leaves truncated JSON or a file with no `layers[]`/`tour[]`. The read discipline is grep-for-sections, which silently returns nothing for an absent key, and the design's answer is presumably "ask the interview fewer structural questions" — i.e. a silent fallback, forbidden by CLAUDE.md ("Never use silent fallback values. Fail explicitly"). The "flag unknowns explicitly" rule is applied only to declined interview answers, never to graph read failures.
- **`gitCommitHash` that is no longer reachable.** Staleness is to be reported "including the commit distance," but the plugin records a hash; after a rebase, squash, shallow clone, or gc that object may not exist in the repo, in which case the distance is uncomputable and the "warn, don't block" policy has no defined behavior. Same for a repo with no commits.
- `meta.json` itself being absent (older plugin version) while the graph exists.

findings.title: The `status: draft` example contradicts the document's own enum rule, and the status→plain-language mapping is undefined
findings.description: "Strip internal vocabulary ... 'Initiative 140 status draft' becomes 'foundational work, in progress.'" uses a status value that Output Conventions declares invalid and gate-rejected ("Invented values such as `draft` are rejected by the gate"), and that the code confirms — `DocumentStatus` is `not_started | in_progress | complete | deferred | deprecated`, with `completed` accepted on read only. The Status and Roadmap fields' actual inputs are those five values; the document never maps `deferred` or `deprecated` initiatives into stakeholder language, which is precisely where "Status is honest" is tested. One canonical mapping table belongs in this architecture, not in slice design.

findings.title: Adding to the bundled analysis pack publishes it through `sq install-commands` regardless of opt-in
findings.description: Delivery claims "no installer, manifest, or CLI change" — true, but only because `install.py::install_commands` iterates *every* subdirectory of `commands/` and copies all `*.md`, while `uninstall_commands` removes only `sq/`. So a new `commands/analysis/understand.md` reaches `~/.claude/commands/analysis/` for every user who runs `sq install-commands`, without `sq skills install analysis`. That is the same directory the pack installer writes to, so the two surfaces overlap on one path. This is pre-existing, but initiative 340's stated principle is "Opt-in, zero default bloat — nothing extra ships with squadron; users pull packs when they need them," and 360 is the initiative that adds the next pack file. Worth an explicit acknowledgement (and a `sq skills uninstall analysis` behavior check) rather than inheriting the ambiguity.
